# Code of Conduct

## Scope

This Code of Conduct applies to every space where Pykachu Go activity happens:
this repository, its issues, pull requests, discussions, the GitHub Pages site,
and any event run by the maintainer with written permission.

## Our pledge

We pledge to make participation in Pykachu Go a harassment-free experience for
everyone, regardless of age, body size, visible or invisible disability,
ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of
experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance,
race, caste, colour, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.

We pledge to act and interact in ways that contribute to an open, welcoming,
diverse, inclusive, and healthy community.

## Expected behaviour

- Use welcoming and inclusive language.
- Respect differing viewpoints, experiences, and levels of expertise.
- Accept constructive criticism gracefully, and give it kindly.
- Focus on what is best for the players and the project, not on personal
  validation.
- Show empathy towards other community members.
- Respect the privacy of teams, players, and event data. Do not post team names,
  security keys, sheet exports, or screenshots containing player information in
  public issues or pull requests.

## Unacceptable behaviour

- Sexualised language or imagery, and sexual attention or advances of any kind.
- Trolling, insulting or derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks.
- Public or private harassment, including publishing others' private information
  without explicit permission.
- Publishing solution keys, puzzle answers, or cheat workarounds during a live
  event.
- Deliberately triggering the anti-cheat systems, or helping others bypass them.
- Any other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a
  professional setting.

## Scope note — this project is permission-gated

Pykachu Go is proprietary work published for academic study and faculty review.
Forking, deploying, or running an event with this software requires prior
written permission from the copyright holder (see [`LICENSE`](../LICENSE)).
Issue and pull request activity on this repository is therefore limited to the
maintainer and explicitly authorised collaborators; unsolicited forks, clones,
or redeployments are handled under that notice, not this document.

## Enforcement responsibilities

The maintainer is responsible for clarifying and enforcing these standards and
will take appropriate and fair corrective action in response to any behaviour
they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive, or harmful. Enforcement
decisions are made by the maintainer alone, because the project has a single
copyright holder.

## Reporting

Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behaviour may be
reported privately to the maintainer at **pranavpaunikar.ml24@sbjit.edu.in**.
Please include links, screenshots, or logs where available. All complaints will
be reviewed promptly and handled confidentially. The maintainer's privacy and
safety will be respected in every report.

## Enforcement guidelines

1. **Correction** — a private, written warning from the maintainer, with clarity
   about the nature of the violation and why the behaviour was inappropriate.
2. **Warning** — a warning with consequences for continued behaviour, including
   a period of no interaction with the people involved.
3. **Temporary ban** — removal of issue, comment, or pull request privileges for
   a defined period.
4. **Permanent ban** — permanent removal of all repository interaction privileges
   and notification of the college administration where the conduct occurred in
   an academic context.
